pairs.scope:
extend NA-37 and a substantial new nonlinear electronic-structure pair

A: `finite-basis-projector-energies-and-variational-electronic-structure`.

Let S be a supplied Hermitian positive-definite overlap matrix, 0 < r < n, and transform to an orthonormal basis using an existing Cholesky/spectral factorization. Define the compact set P_r = {P=P*, P²=P, tr P=r}. Input finite h=h*, a self-adjoint real-linear map G on Hermitian matrices, and optional real C² functional E_xc on a neighborhood of P_r. Define E(P)=tr(hP)+1/2 tr(PG(P))+E_xc(P) and its Hermitian Frobenius-gradient F(P)=h+G(P)+grad E_xc(P). The conditional finite-basis HF case is E_xc=0 with a supplied symmetry-compatible Coulomb/exchange tensor; the KS-like case is an explicitly supplied density map and differentiable chosen functional. These are mathematical definitions, not assertions of physical exactness. Prove a global minimizer exists, first variation along P(t)=e^{tK}Pe^{-tK} yields [F(P),P]=0, and a sufficient positive tangent-Hessian condition gives an isolated strict local minimizer modulo orbital gauge. A commutator-zero point need not be a minimum and need not occupy the lowest r eigenvalues. Do not silently equate stationarity and Aufbau SCF.

Also include the finite-temperature density domain 0<=D<=I, tr D=r with continuous endpoint convention 0 log 0=0 and entropy term beta^(-1) tr(D log D+(I-D)log(I-D)). Prove compact-domain minimizer existence; on the interior derive the Fermi–Dirac stationarity equation with chemical potential chosen for the trace, and prove uniqueness of that chemical potential for a fixed finite Hermitian F and 0<r<n. This does not prove uniqueness of a self-consistent density for a nonconvex energy. PC-VAR owns spectral trace derivative and endpoint-continuity suppliers; generic constrained KKT/prox comes from optimization owner.

For nested trial spaces, the finite-basis infimum decreases toward the infimum over their union; equality with a continuum infimum additionally requires density in the energy topology and continuity/liminf hypotheses, each proved for the chosen functional. No general Coulomb HF/DFT existence theorem is smuggled into this statement. Source-model error stays separate.

NA-37 amendment, no extra pair: for a normalized Ritz vector u with Rayleigh quotient mu and residual rho=||(A-mu)u||, prove dist(mu,spec A)<=rho. If a specific simple target eigenvalue is separated by certified gap delta from all others, prove sin(angle(u,e))<=rho/delta using spectral expansion; add an upper energy bound from min–max. A residual alone cannot identify the lowest eigenvalue. For a ground state on a compact-resolvent form domain carry the actual form/duality norm and continuum regularity, not the finite-matrix formula verbatim.

Proof route: bounded closed polynomial projector set is compact; Weierstrass; differentiate matrix traces and commutator curves; characterize all tangent directions as [K,P]; Taylor on local graph charts; spectral expansion for residuals; monotone infima plus explicit approximants for trial density. Same-frontier new suppliers owned PC-VAR: projector tangent/graph chart and gauge invariance, compactness, energy derivative/Hessian. Reuse canonical matrix differential, Courant–Fischer and optimization-owner retraction items.

B: two-level nonlinear projector with a stationary maximum; overlapping basis with ill-conditioned S; incomplete CI energy above its finite Hamiltonian ground energy; nested trial energies; nonsmooth chosen E_xc where the C² theorem fails.

Sources to inspect before authoring: Cancès–Le Bris, Can we outperform the DIIS approach for electronic structure calculations?, https://doi.org/10.1002/1097-461X(2000)79:2%3C82::AID-QUA3%3E3.0.CO;2-I . Citations here are candidate source locations, not completed reading evidence.

pairs.scope:
genuinely-new nonlinear projector iteration, with certified safeguards

A: `self-consistent-projector-iterations-and-certified-mixing`.

Define F(P)=F(P)* and Phi(P)=spectral projector onto the r lowest eigenvalues, only on a declared neighborhood with uniform occupied/unoccupied gap g>0. Define undamped SCF P_{k+1}=Phi(P_k), a distinct relaxed density iteration D_{k+1}=(1-alpha)D_k+alpha Phi(D_k) on a closed admissible Hermitian density set, and a finite-memory DIIS least-squares proposal with singular-system fallback, coefficient/budget cap, and accept/reject rule. Relaxed D is generally not an idempotent projector; keep domains explicit.

Prove block spectral-projector differentiability and Lipschitz bounds from a common separating resolvent contour (or Sylvester off-diagonal equation). If a complete invariant metric neighborhood has Lip(Phi)<=q<1, prove geometric SCF convergence and error<=||P-Phi(P)||/(1-q). For differentiable relaxed map, a certified induced-norm bound ||(1-alpha)I+alpha DPhi||<=q<1 on the whole neighborhood gives the corresponding result. Damping alone is not a proof of contraction. Given inexact Phi evaluations with deterministic error eta_k, prove e_{k+1}<=q e_k+eta_k and the explicit convolution bound. DIIS convergence is claimed only for an actual residual-decreasing safeguarded scheme with a proved contractive baseline and enforceable error budget; bare DIIS gets no universal theorem. Level shifts change the map and require a fixed-point-equivalence proof under their stated eigenvalue ordering.

Full proof route: contour identity and resolvent identity; Weyl gap persistence and uniform inverse estimates; Banach fixed point; telescoping inexact recurrence; accept DIIS only if certified candidate error/residual gives the stipulated contraction, otherwise use baseline. Same-frontier suppliers PC-SCF: block/cluster projector derivative (simple-eigenvalue canonical result is insufficient), computable gap persistence and resolvent bound, level-shift equivalence, safeguard theorem. Generic Anderson acceleration if optimization owner supplies it is reused, not redefined.

B: explicit two-cycle of SCF; zero-gap projector discontinuity; contractive affine response toy model; residual certificate with additive eigensolve tolerance; density mixing leaving the projector manifold; DIIS singular Gram fallback. Candidate sources: Cancès–Le Bris above; Rohwedder–Schneider, DIIS convergence analysis, https://doi.org/10.1007/s00211-011-0401-3 ; Walker–Ni Anderson acceleration, https://doi.org/10.1137/10078356X . Author must inspect exact theorems rather than cite titles as proof.

pairs.scope:
genuinely-new continuation through simple folds

A: `pseudo-arclength-continuation-and-fold-certificates`.

Input F:R^(n+1)->R^n, C²/C³ on an explicit tube, residual/derivative evaluation errors, orientation, step h, and a finite work budget. At regular curve points rank DF=n, compute a normalized tangent t in ker DF, predict z+h t, and correct augmented G(z)=(F(z), t_old^T(z-z_pred)) by existing Newton with a failure branch. Prove the bordered derivative is invertible when rank DF=n and t_old has nonzero component along current tangent; give inverse-norm/angular bounds. Prove predictor defect O(h²), Newton local quadratic correction, local branch uniqueness and error in terms of residual/inverse bounds. At a simple fold of F(x,lambda), require rank F_x=n-1 with right/left nullvectors v,w and w^T F_lambda !=0, w^T F_xx[v,v] !=0. Prove local fold parameterization and lambda'' !=0; pseudo-arclength traverses it. No global branch completeness from finite steps.

Same-frontier suppliers PC-CONT: oriented nullspace/bordered inverse bound, quantitative curve charts, fold Lyapunov–Schmidt reduction with complement solve and scalar Taylor remainder; canonical parametrized IFT and Newton are reused. Interval enclosure/certification consumes optimization-owner validated numerics if provided; otherwise author its needed contraction enclosure locally. B: x²-lambda=0; lambda parameter continuation fails at fold; tangent-angle failure; disconnected branch missed by a valid local trace. Sources: Keller pseudo-arclength chapter https://doi.org/10.1016/B978-0-12-060350-1.50014-0 ; Allgower–Georg, Numerical Continuation Methods https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-61257-2 . pairs.scope:
genuinely-new local bifurcation calculation and its full prerequisites

A: `local-bifurcation-normal-forms-and-numerical-certificates`.

For supplied finite-dimensional C^k ODE x'=f(x,lambda), distinguish certified equilibrium eigenvalue crossing from a nonlinear bifurcation theorem. Include scalar fold/transcritical/pitchfork normal forms only with exact derivative/nondegeneracy and symmetry assumptions. Include a simple Hopf theorem with one simple pair +/-i omega, omega>0, all other eigenvalues off the imaginary axis, transverse crossing, sufficient smoothness (declare k>=5), and nonzero first Lyapunov coefficient computed from multilinear second/third derivatives using a fixed normalization and sign convention. Prove existence/side/stability of the small local periodic branch. Finite interval enclosures for eigenpair, derivative and coefficient certify only these local hypotheses. No claim an eigenvalue plot alone proves a Hopf or global dynamics.

Full proof route obligation: local spectral splitting, finite-dimensional parameter-dependent C^k center manifold with actual invariance equation and remainder bounds; near-identity homological polynomial elimination on the two-dimensional center subspace; polar/Poincaré return map expansion; IFT solves its nonzero-radius fixed point; return-map derivative proves orbital stability together with transverse spectral stability. This is established missing mathematics, not an open problem. All these bodies must be authored as separate typed suppliers under PC-BIF before its theorem. If the owner instead uses Lyapunov–Schmidt periodic boundary-value reduction, its inverse on complement, time-phase gauge and remainder estimates must be fully proved locally, replacing—not merely citing—the center-manifold route. No external theorem fallback.

B: supercritical/subcritical Hopf in planar cubic examples; imaginary eigenvalues but zero Lyapunov coefficient; pitchfork destroyed by broken symmetry; interval coefficient enclosure containing zero gives inconclusive result. Sources: Kuznetsov Elements of Applied Bifurcation Theory https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4757-3978-7 ; Scholarpedia Hopf bifurcation overview https://www.scholarpedia.org/article/Andronov-Hopf_bifurcation (overview is orientation, not full proof supplier). Reading pending.

pairs.scope:
genuinely-new periodic-orbit computation and Floquet certificates

A: `periodic-orbit-shooting-collocation-and-floquet-error`.

Define shooting unknown (x0,T) with residual phi_T(x0)-x0 plus phase condition; multiple shooting and periodic collocation use time-owner algorithms. An autonomous periodic orbit has unit Floquet multiplier; impose phase transversality and simplicity of this unit multiplier so the augmented Newton derivative is invertible. Prove augmented-Jacobian characterization; residual-to-orbit local error and discretization error with explicit inverse/time sensitivity constants. Define monodromy by the variational IVP; compute Floquet multipliers with canonical Schur/eigensolver. Prove perturbation enclosure for separated simple multipliers (canonical left/right conditioning), cluster enclosures where necessary, and certification of orbital stability only when all nontrivial multiplier enclosures lie strictly inside the unit disk. No stability conclusion from finite precision values touching it.

Suppliers PC-PER: periodic phase quotient and bordered inverse; time owner flow/variational error; linear owner matrix/eigensolver perturbation; PC-BIF local existence if consumed. B: planar oscillator with phase singularity; stable van der Pol orbit conditional on a validated local enclosure; close/unit multipliers and inconclusive certificate; discretization-induced unstable multiplier. Sources: Doedel et al AUTO documentation https://indy.cs.concordia.ca/auto/ ; Kuznetsov above. Reading pending; software manual is an algorithm specification, not proof replacement.

A: `nystrom-product-integration-and-fredholm-error`.

On X=C([a,b]), define K u(x)=integral k(x,y)u(y)dy, smooth continuous-kernel Nyström with specified quadrature and reconstructed K_n, and product integration k(x,y)=s(x,y)a(x,y) with a specified weak singularity s and exact/computably enclosed product weights. The equations are (I-K)u=f and (I-K_n)u_n=f_n. In the operator-norm route prove ||K-K_n||<=epsilon_n in the stated X/operator spaces; if ||(I-K)^-1|| epsilon_n<1, derive discrete inverse bound and ||u-u_n|| <= ||(I-K_n)^-1|| (||f-f_n||+||(K-K_n)u||). **Do not assert norm convergence on C for arbitrary point-sampling quadrature**: standard Nyström commonly needs the collectively compact route. Prove pointwise consistency and collective compactness (uniform boundedness/equicontinuity), then uniform discrete invertibility from contradiction/compact subsequences and continuous injectivity. Error rate uses quadrature of k(x,.)u(.), with its actual regularity, not all continuous unit-ball functions. Include a singular-kernel product-integration instance with weight stability and consistency proved, not assumed.

genuinely-new volume scattering computation

A: `volume-integral-scattering-and-partial-wave-error`.

For bounded D in R³ and supplied bounded compactly supported q, define K_k u(x)=integral_D exp(ik|x-y|)/(4pi|x-y|) q(y)u(y)dy on a declared L² or continuous space, k real fixed. Prove boundedness and compactness by truncating the singularity, estimating the discarded small-ball kernel by Schur bounds, and compact approximation of the remaining continuous kernel. For ||K_k||<1 prove Born/Neumann truncation error <=||K_k||^(m+1)||f||/(1-||K_k||). Otherwise existence/stability requires injectivity plus Fredholm (or PDE-owner actual scattering uniqueness under stated q/sign/radiation assumptions). Discretize using PC-NYST-compatible singular product/volume quadrature and prove far-field functional error from the solution estimate and quadrature error. For radial inputs derive the partial-wave radial BVP by explicit spherical harmonic expansion, regular-origin boundary conditions, outer matching and angular-mode truncation bound under a stated coefficient/analyticity regime. Resonance detection uses isolated complex-pole/operator analytic-Fredholm proofs only if fully supplied; a determinant nearly zero is diagnostic, not a theorem.

PC-SCAT owns kernel compactness, volume/far-field maps, radial transform/error; PC-NYST owns discretization spectral clusters; PDE owner owns outgoing uniqueness when actually consumed; linear owner singular quadrature/special transforms; PC-SFUN supplies scaled spherical Bessel evaluations. pairs.scope:
genuinely-new stable special-function algorithms

A: `stable-special-function-recurrences-and-certified-evaluation`.

Do not reauthor gamma/Bessel definitions. Reuse existing `def-euler-gamma-function`, `thm-stirling-formula-gamma`, `thm-gamma-functional-equation` only after exact statement inspection. Define finite-budget domain-partitioned evaluators for exp-scaled Bessel/modified Bessel and Airy, Fresnel sine/cosine integrals, gamma/log-gamma, erf/erfc, and a representative hypergeometric function. Each branch declares real/complex domain and branch cut, series/quadrature/continued fraction/asymptotic formula, scaling convention, remainder certificate, absolute/relative tolerance, and failure branch. No relative-error promise at zeros or cancellation without a conditioning factor.

Essential substantial new methods: forward/backward three-term recurrence; Miller backward recurrence with a normalization and **explicit minimal/dominant separation hypotheses**; derive terminal-data contamination coefficient and finite-N truncation bound from two fundamental recurrence solutions and their discrete Wronskian. A stable direction is theorem/domain specific. Continued fractions use a proved convergent/remainder bound for the chosen coefficients; divergent asymptotic series use finite truncation with an independently proved remainder, not convergence. Include interval-enclosed power-series/geometric-tail evaluator and scaled asymptotic branch; show representation identities and overlap consistency on declared ranges. Prove recurrence/roundoff error amplification by inhomogeneous fundamental solutions. Algorithms may return inconclusive when the derived bound is too weak.

genuinely-new finite Gaussian integral algorithms

A: `gaussian-basis-integral-recurrences-and-boys-error`.

Input finitely many Cartesian Gaussian primitives (polynomial times exp(-a|x-A|²), a>0), real centers and contraction coefficients. Define overlap, kinetic, attraction and two-electron Coulomb integrals as mathematical integrals. Prove absolute convergence including Coulomb singularities; Gaussian product theorem by completing squares; polynomial derivative/raising recurrences by differentiation under an explicit integrable dominating function. Reduce Coulomb integrals using 1/r=(2/sqrt(pi)) integral_0^infinity exp(-t²r²)dt with justified Tonelli and a change of variables to Boys F_m(T)=integral_0^1 t^(2m) exp(-Tt²)dt, m>=0,T>=0. Define finite primitive/contracted integral procedure with a declared recurrence ordering, memoization/work model and error budget. Establish Boys Taylor remainder for small T, positive quadrature enclosure on bounded T, and scaled incomplete-gamma/large-T tail bounds. Prove upward/downward recurrence error amplification and domain-based direction switch. Screening skips a block only with a proved bound (e.g. Coulomb Cauchy–Schwarz), and reports total discarded integral/energy bound rather than claiming exact sparsity.

pairs.scope:
genuinely-new periodic lattice-sum algorithm and error separation

A: `ewald-periodic-potentials-and-particle-mesh-error`.

On a specified 3D torus, finitely many distinct positions x_i and real charges q_i with sum q_i=0 define the mean-zero periodic Poisson distribution -Delta u=4pi(sum q_i delta_xi). Prove the Fourier distribution solution with zero mode fixed and the Gaussian Ewald decomposition of its off-source values/renormalized self energy. Specify the lattice shape, self subtraction, Gaussian parameter alpha, real/reciprocal cutoffs, output convention and arithmetic model. The naive Coulomb lattice sum is conditional; the periodic mean-zero definition controls the summation convention. Prove absolute convergence of the split sums, alpha independence, explicit Gaussian real-tail/reciprocal-tail bounds using lattice shell counts, and differentiated force bounds away from collisions. Include other boundary conventions only by separate explicit formula/proof.

For particle-mesh Ewald specify charge assignment degree/window, periodic grid, discrete Fourier solver, deconvolution restrictions, force differentiation and self correction. Prove error as real cutoff + reciprocal cutoff + assignment/aliasing + mesh differentiation + arithmetic, with actual window Fourier-decay/smoothness assumptions; O(N log N) FFT work alone is not an accuracy theorem. Point-source potentials are singular: any uniform field error is on a collision-free evaluation set, or is stated for a regularized source norm. N-body time integration, thermodynamic limits and singular mean-field limits remain separate.

Same-frontier PC-EWALD suppliers: Gaussian Poisson summation (reuse canonical Poisson theorem if its hypotheses fit), torus distribution Green function and zero mode, lattice shell Gaussian estimates, self limit, assignment Fourier aliases and force derivative bounds. Linear owner FFT; PDE owner periodic Poisson if it supplies the exact torus distribution interface; biology owner PIC consumes only the solver guarantee under matching regularization. B: neutral dipole cell, nonneutral zero-mode obstruction, alpha tradeoff at fixed tolerance, source collision, energy/force consistency.
